recipe.name: Fudgy Sourdough Discard Brownies (Easy 8x8 Recipe)
recipe.summary: Do you have extra sourdough discard sitting in your fridge? Don't throw it away! These Sourdough Discard Brownies are the ultimate way to use your leftover starter.

equipment.name: 8x8 inch pan
equipment.notes: grease and line with parchment paper

instructions.name: Step 1: Prep the Oven and Pan Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease an 8x8-inch baking pan and line it with parchment paper, leaving a bit of overhang on the sides. This makes it incredibly easy to lift the brownies out of the pan once they cool.

Step 2: Mix the Wet In a large mixing bowl, beat together the 3 eggs, ½ cup of sourdough discard, ¼ cup of oil, ¼ cup of melted butter, and 1 tsp of vanilla extract. Whisk until the mixture is smooth and fully combined.

Step 3: Add the Dry Ingredients Whisk in the ½ cup of flour, ½ tsp of baking powder, ¼ tsp of salt, and ⅓ cup of cocoa powder. Stir gently until the dry ingredients are just incorporated into the wet batter. Be careful not to overmix, as overmixing can make the brownies cakey instead of fudgy.
Step 4: Fold in the Chocolate Chips For the final step, grab your spatula and gently fold in the 1 cup of chocolate chips until they are evenly distributed throughout the thick batter.

Step 5: Bake to Perfection Pour the batter into your prepared 8x8 pan and smooth the top. Bake for 25 to 30 minutes. Test the center with a toothpick; they are done when the toothpick comes out clean or with just a few moist crumbs attached.
Step 6: Cool and Serve Let the brownies cool completely in the pan before lifting them out using the parchment paper edges. Slice into squares and enjoy!
Baker's Tips for Success
The Toothpick Test: For an extra fudgy texture, pull the brownies out when the toothpick has a few moist crumbs. If it comes out completely wet, they need a few more minutes
Parchment Paper Hack: Lining the pan prevents the brownies from sticking to the bottom and allows you to make perfectly clean cuts on a cutting board later.
Sourdough Hydration: This recipe is optimized for a standard 100% hydration starter (equal parts flour and water by weight).

Sourdough Hydration: This recipe is optimized for a standard 100% hydration starter (equal parts flour and water by weight).

recipe.notes:
Chef's Notes & Troubleshooting
🥣 Sourdough Discard Tips
  • Age of Discard: You can use fresh discard or starter that has been sitting in the fridge for up to two weeks. Older discard will add a deeper, more complex flavor profile, while fresh discard keeps the taste very mild.
  • Temperature: Try to bring your discard to room temperature for about 15-20 minutes before mixing. Cold discard can shock the melted butter, causing it to prematurely solidify and clump in the batter.
🧈 Butter Textures Matter
  • Why Two States?: This recipe uniquely uses both softened and melted butter. Melted butter creates that ultra-dense, fudgy texture, while the softened butter provides just enough structure so the brownies don't turn into complete puddle-like grease. Make sure your melted butter is warm, not piping hot, so it doesn't accidentally cook the eggs.
🍫 Customizing the Sweetness
  • No Added Sugar: Because this specific recipe relies entirely on the chocolate chips for sweetness (instead of adding extra granulated sugar), the type of chocolate you choose matters. For a sweeter brownie, use milk chocolate chips. For a dark, rich, adult-style brownie, use 60% or 70% bittersweet chocolate chips.
⏱️ How to Avoid Cakey Brownies
  • Watch the Clock: Oven calibration varies wildly. Start checking your brownies at the 22-minute mark.
  • The Toothpick Test Rule: For cake, you want a clean toothpick. For fudgy brownies, you actually want a few moist crumbs attached to the toothpick. If the toothpick comes out completely clean, they are slightly overbaked (but will still taste delicious!).
📦 Storage & Freezing Instructions
  • Room Temperature: Store baked brownies in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3 days.
  • Refrigerator: Keeping them in the fridge extends their shelf life to 6 days and makes them incredibly dense and chewy.
  • Freezing: Wrap individual squares tightly in plastic wrap, then place them in a freezer-safe Ziploc bag. Freeze for up to 3 months. Thaw at room temperature for 1 hour or microwave for 15 seconds for a warm, gooey treat.

recipe.name: Zero Guilt Keto Chocolate Donuts
recipe.summary: A rich, fudgy, low-carb, and nut-free donut recipe packed with whey protein and deep cocoa flavor.

equipment.name: donut pans
equipment.notes: a silicone donut pan or any small ring-shaped pan will work

instructions.name: Baking the Donuts
Prep Your Oven: Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C). Thoroughly grease a standard 6-cavity donut pan with non-stick spray or butter. [1, 2, 3]

Combine the Dry Ingredients: In a medium-sized bowl, vigorously whisk together your coconut flour, whey protein powder, cocoa powder, granular sweetener, baking powder, and salt until completely free of lumps. [1, 2, 3]

Whisk the Wet Ingredients: In a separate container, beat the eggs. Slowly pour in the melted butter, cooled brewed coffee, and vanilla extract, whisking continuously to avoid cooking the eggs. [1, 2, 3]

Mix the Batter: Pour your liquid mixture directly into the dry ingredients. Stir with a spatula until a smooth, uniform batter forms. Note: Coconut flour absorbs liquid rapidly, so let the batter sit for 2 minutes to thicken up. [1, 2, 3]
Fill the Pan: Spoon the batter evenly into your prepared donut cavities, or pipe it in using a plastic storage bag with the corner snipped off. Smooth down the tops with a damp finger. [1, 2, 3]
Bake to Perfection: Bake for 15 to 18 minutes. They are ready when the tops feel firm to a gentle touch and a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean. [1, 2, 3]
Cool Safely: Allow the donuts to cool inside the pan for 10 minutes. Carefully invert the pan over a wire rack to release them, letting them cool completely before adding any optional glaze. [1, 2]
(Recipe inspired by keto baking traditions)
Glazing the Donuts
Sift the Dry: Sift the powdered sweetener and cocoa powder into a small bowl to remove lumps.
Combine Liquids: Stir in the melted butter, vanilla extract, and 1 tablespoon of the warm heavy cream.
Adjust Thickness: Whisk until completely smooth. If the glaze is too thick, add the remaining heavy cream a few drops at a time until it reaches a thick, pourable consistency.
Dip the Donuts: Dip the tops of your fully cooled donuts directly into the glaze, then place them back on a wire rack to set for 10 minutes.

Sift the Dry: Sift the powdered sweetener and cocoa powder into a small bowl to remove lumps.

Adjust Thickness: Whisk until completely smooth. If the glaze is too thick, add the remaining heavy cream a few drops at a time until it reaches a thick, pourable consistency.

recipe.notes:
• Let the Batter Rest: Coconut flour acts like a sponge and absorbs liquid rapidly. After mixing the wet and dry ingredients, let the batter sit on your counter for 2 full minutes. It will thicken up significantly, making it much easier to pipe or spoon into your donut pan.
  • The Coffee Secret: Do not skip the brewed coffee! The coffee does not make the donuts taste like mocha; instead, the acidity and flavor compounds chemically intensify the cocoa powder, making the donuts taste incredibly rich and fudgy. Ensure the coffee is cooled to room temperature before mixing, or you risk scrambling the eggs.
  • Protein Powder Choice: For the best texture, use a whey protein isolate or a whey-casein blend. Avoid using pure plant-based protein powders (like pea or hemp) in this specific recipe, as they absorb too much moisture and will make your donuts dense and dry.
  • Nut-Free Alternative: This recipe is naturally nut-free because it uses coconut flour instead of almond flour. If you are baking for someone with a severe coconut allergy, please note that coconut flour cannot be swapped 1:1 with any other flour.
  • Storage & Freezing: Store leftover glazed donuts in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 5 days. You can also freeze unglazed donuts for up to 3 months; simply thaw them at room temperature and apply fresh glaze before serving.

recipe.name: Chicken Piccata with broccoli

instructions.text: Cook pasta, according to instructions. Add salt to water before it boils. Drain and set aside.
Heat oil in pan, add chicken, salt and pepper. Cook chicken about 4-5 minutes, on each side. Remove and set aside.

Make piccata sauce. Add a bit more oil to pan, add garlic and cook for 1 minute. Add chicken broth, capers, lemon juice, salt, and pepper. Cook for 2-3 minutes, or until sauce is reduced by half. Swirl in cold butter until sauce thickens.
Add chicken back to pan, and spoon sauce on top.
In a separate pan, heat oil. Add broccoli florets, season with salt and pepper. Cook 5-6 minutes. Serve with chicken, picatta sauce and linguine. Garnish with lemon

recipe.notes: A classic dish featuring capers in a lemon butter sauce and spooned over chicken.  Sure to be a huge hit among guests!  Add linguine and broccoli.  This classic dish is great with fish too!!

recipe.name: Salmon Cobb Salad

instructions.text: Make the avocado dressing in a blender.  Add avocado, oil, lemon juice, salt and water.  Blend until smooth. Set aside
Heat oven to 400 degrees.  Brush salmon with oil, salt, pepper, dill and lemon juice.  Place on baking sheet and bake for 10-15 minutes, or until salmon flakes easily with fork.
Place potatoes and asparagus on a separate baking sheet, add oil, salt and pepper.  Bake 25-30 minutes or until fork tender.
Serve salmon, eggs (sprinkle with paprika), potatoes, asparagus and drizzle with avocado dressing.

Serve salmon, eggs (sprinkle with paprika), potatoes, asparagus and drizzle with avocado dressing.

recipe.notes: A version of a classic Cobb salad made with salmon, asparagus, avocado dressing, potatoes, and boiled eggs.  Surprise your guests with this yummy Cobb salad!

recipe.name: Kale Salad with Pistachios
recipe.author_bio: Culinary Chef, Pilates and Yoga Instructor, Multi-Sport Athlete

instructions.text: Wash and chop kale
In a large mixing bowl, add kale and olive oil.  Start to mix using either your hands or tongs and rub oil into kale until it turns bright green.
Add the lemon juice, nutritional yeast, garlic and salt.  Continue to mix until well blended.
Add pistachios and serve.
Refrigerate any leftovers for 3-4 days.
